text: Decide the native ABI entry mechanism (syscall instruction per operation, shared submission page with rare doorbell syscalls, or vDSO-like trampolines) and set a maximum count of kernel entry points.
rationale: Entry mechanism defines syscall-overhead budgets and the size of the surface that must remain stable for decades.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Define the ABI freeze gate: golden binary compatibility test suite, fuzz corpus, documented semantics for every entry point, and a policy for adding versus changing entry points.
rationale: Without explicit freeze criteria the V1 'stable native SDK' claim has no verifiable meaning.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the Linux personality implementation depth for each milestone: in-kernel Linux syscall path retained (Phase A), in-kernel translation onto native primitives, or gVisor-style userspace personality, with syscall overhead measured per option.
rationale: Linux compatibility overhead is a tracked 1.0 metric and each option locks in different maintenance and security trade-offs.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Prototype mapping a Linux process to a native Component and its file descriptors to capabilities, and decide whether Linux processes are first-class components or a separate personality-managed construct.
rationale: This determines whether resource domains, tracing and permissions apply uniformly to compatibility software.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether the native compositor implements Wayland protocols directly or hosts a nested compatibility compositor, and whether X11 arrives only via Xwayland.
rationale: Linux GUI applications must feel native, and the compositor architecture cannot easily switch later.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether xdg-desktop-portal becomes the bridge through which Linux applications reach the native capability-based file chooser, clipboard and screen-share grants.
rationale: Portals are the existing sandbox interface Linux apps already speak, and reusing them avoids inventing a second compatibility permission model.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the level of glibc and systemd emulation the Linux personality provides (real systemd, a systemd-compatible service manager, or none) based on a survey of the top 200 Linux desktop applications' actual dependencies.
rationale: Compatibility is a product, and its scope must be set from evidence about what applications require.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether 32-bit x86 Linux and Win32 binaries are supported in the personalities, given that a large share of Windows games are 32-bit.
rationale: Dropping 32-bit silently kills the gaming objective; keeping it costs kernel ABI surface and personality effort.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether the Windows personality runs Wine over the Linux personality (fast path to results) or Wine ported directly onto the native ABI, with overhead measured on a fixed game benchmark set.
rationale: Layering Wine on Linux compatibility doubles translation overhead but layering on native requires porting Wine's Unix assumptions.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Publish a research finding on anti-cheat feasibility that states which kernel-level anti-cheat systems cannot work under the capability model and are therefore out of 1.0 scope.
rationale: Setting expectations early prevents a gaming objective from silently expanding into kernel compromises.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether a KVM-backed virtual machine personality is an officially supported fallback for Linux or Windows software the personalities cannot run.
rationale: A VM fallback changes the compatibility promise and must integrate with the same launcher, clipboard and file chooser to avoid the 'obvious VM' failure.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Spike exposing Mesa/Vulkan to a native component through Surface and Buffer capabilities without ambient /dev/dri access, and decide the GPU userspace strategy from the result.
rationale: GPU is the hardest blocker, and the native graphics abstraction is unproven until a real driver stack works behind it.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the NVIDIA support stance for 1.0 (open kernel modules with NVK/Mesa, proprietary userspace via compatibility, or unsupported) after evaluating each against the capability model.
rationale: Proprietary userspace drivers assume ambient device access and may be impossible to fit behind capabilities.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the compositor process architecture (monolithic vs split display/scene/input components) by prototyping crash-and-rebind and measuring input-to-photon latency of each.
rationale: Crash recovery and latency requirements pull in opposite directions and the split cannot be changed after the UI protocol depends on it.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide that explicit GPU synchronization (timeline semaphores / drm_syncobj) is mandatory for all native surfaces from the first compositor, with no implicit-sync path.
rationale: Retrofitting explicit sync later is the exact pain Wayland went through and the native protocol should not repeat it.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the compositor rendering backend policy (Vulkan-only, or Vulkan plus GL fallback) based on the selected target hardware list.
rationale: A single backend reduces maintenance but may exclude older target laptops chosen for V2.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Prototype the native UI protocol as retained scene graph transmitted over channels, client-rendered buffers, and a hybrid, and choose by measured latency, memory and toolkit ergonomics.
rationale: The UI protocol shape determines accessibility, automation and remote-surface capabilities and is nearly as permanent as the kernel ABI.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether to build a new UI toolkit or adopt and adapt an existing Rust toolkit and renderer, with an evaluation matrix covering accessibility tree output and declarative model fit.
rationale: Toolkit effort is a multi-year cost and must be scoped before the four V0.5 demo applications are started.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the text stack (HarfBuzz/FreeType reuse vs Rust shaping and rasterization) and whether shaping runs in-process or in a shared text service component.
rationale: Text rendering underpins every native application and a shared service changes the isolation and latency model.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the IDL (adopt WIT, adopt FIDL, adopt Cap'n Proto schema, or design new) using a written evaluation against ownership transfer, capability passing, versioning, streams and multi-language codegen.
rationale: The IDL is the language every platform interface is written in and switching after V1 would invalidate every generated binding.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Benchmark wire encodings (in-place zero-copy access vs compact encode/decode) including receiver-side validation cost, and decide the message representation.
rationale: Encoding cost is a fixed tax on every IPC message and validation cost is a security requirement that must be measured, not assumed.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Exercise the interface versioning scheme by evolving one real interface through three incompatible revisions in the V0 prototype before the scheme is frozen.
rationale: Versioning designs look correct on paper and fail on first real evolution; the failure must happen before commitments.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether Wasm components and native components share one IDL and one interface registry or maintain a mapping layer between WIT and the native IDL.
rationale: A shared IDL fulfils the 'participate naturally' goal but constrains the native IDL to WIT's evolution.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Evaluate Wasm runtimes (Wasmtime, WAMR, others) for instantiation latency, memory footprint and capability binding, and decide the system runtime.
rationale: Wasm plugins must be cheap enough to be the default extension mechanism or they will be bypassed by native code.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Benchmark candidate filesystems (btrfs, bcachefs, ZFS, XFS with reflink) for snapshot creation, clone, checksum overhead, dedup and crash consistency, and choose the initial storage substrate.
rationale: System generations and dev environment snapshots depend on the substrate and migrating user data between filesystems later is a 1.0-blocking risk.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the content-addressed store layout (Nix-style store paths, OSTree-style object repository, or chunk-based casync-like) after measuring dedup ratio and update size on a realistic package set.
rationale: The store layout is shared by packages, generations and dev environments and is effectively a persistent on-disk format.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the content hash algorithm and chunking strategy (sha256 vs BLAKE3, whole-object vs content-defined chunking) for the store.
rationale: Hash identity appears in package identifiers and signatures and cannot be changed without re-identifying every object.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the disk encryption layer (dm-crypt/LUKS block level, fscrypt file level, or filesystem-native) and its interaction with snapshots and content-addressed dedup.
rationale: Encryption choice constrains filesystem choice and per-user data isolation, and must precede the storage ADR.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the bootloader (systemd-boot, GRUB, custom Rust UEFI stub, or unified kernel images) based on generation selection, Secure Boot signing chain and measured boot requirements.
rationale: Boot-time generation rollback is a first-class feature and the bootloader must support it natively.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the early-boot design for locating the content store and selected generation (initramfs contents, kernel command line, or bootloader-passed manifest).
rationale: Generation booting only works if early boot can find immutable objects before any mutable state is trusted.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Prototype scheduling-intent support as an extension of the existing scheduler class, as a sched_ext BPF scheduler, and as a new scheduler class, and choose by measured latency for audio and compositor workloads.
rationale: Intent-aware scheduling is a core promise and the implementation route sets the divergence cost against upstream.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether ResourceDomain is implemented over cgroup v2 controllers or as native accounting, with measured overhead per domain.
rationale: Reusing cgroups preserves maturity but may leak Linux semantics into the native model the baseline forbids.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the tracing substrate (ftrace/perf ring buffers vs new per-object event ring) and set a measured overhead ceiling (e.g. under 1% CPU with tracing enabled).
rationale: Observability is architecture, so its cost must be bounded before every primitive is instrumented.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the trace export format (Perfetto-compatible, OpenTelemetry-compatible, or native) so existing analysis tooling can be reused.
rationale: A private format forces the project to build analysis UIs before developers can use the tracing at all.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Select the Linux base version and LTS alignment for the fork and decide the upstream tracking strategy (periodic rebase vs merge) with a measured rebase cost after the first six months.
rationale: Fork maintenance is a permanent cost and the tracking strategy determines when Phase D divergence becomes affordable.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Run a Rust-in-kernel viability spike identifying which Linux internal subsystems (mm, scheduler, DRM, VFS) need new Rust abstractions for the native platform, and decide the C-versus-Rust boundary.
rationale: Rust-first is stated policy but the binding gap to Linux internals is unknown and dictates early velocity.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether an IOMMU is a hard hardware requirement for user-space drivers and DMA-capable MemoryObjects, and what degradation applies on systems without one.
rationale: Without IOMMU protection a user-space driver can DMA over the kernel, undermining the entire isolation story.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Prototype a user-space driver for one USB class and one Bluetooth controller (VFIO or native device capability) and measure interrupt latency and throughput against the in-kernel driver.
rationale: The user-space driver strategy is a stated direction but its performance cost is unknown for the classes proposed.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether native NetworkConnection objects wrap the kernel TCP/IP stack directly or pass through a userspace network service component, with measured throughput and latency.
rationale: Networking must retain Linux maturity while enforcing network capabilities, and the placement decision shapes the firewall and VPN design.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether PipeWire is adopted as the native audio server or a native audio object service is built with PipeWire as a compatibility client, after measuring achievable round-trip latency for each.
rationale: Audio is the strictest latency consumer and duplicating PipeWire violates the do-not-replace-mature-systems principle unless justified by measurement.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Write a threat model document enumerating attacker classes (malicious app, compromised component, malicious peripheral, evil maid, remote) before capability, personality and storage security designs are frozen.
rationale: Security decisions in every workstream need a shared reference for what they are defending against.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the identity and login model (local accounts, hardware-backed keys, session capability roots) and how a login session becomes the root capability holder.
rationale: The capability tree must have a defined root or the desktop shell ends up with ambient authority.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the signing scheme and trust model for packages and generations (key algorithm, TUF-style metadata, key rotation) before the first public repository.
rationale: Signing formats are embedded in every published package and cannot be rotated cheaply after users depend on them.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Measure delta versus full-generation update sizes on the chosen store format and decide the update delivery mechanism.
rationale: Update bandwidth and rollback speed determine whether generations feel first-class or burdensome.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Investigate whether application-state restore in system history is achievable through checkpointing, application-cooperative state interfaces, or not at all, and scope it as a 1.0 non-goal if evidence is negative.
rationale: The baseline names it a long-term ambition and the roadmap needs a decision on whether any of it lands by 1.0.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether Wayland-style ABI stability applies to Layer 2 core platform interfaces at V1 or only at 1.0, and publish the deprecation policy for each stability layer.
rationale: Developers building on V1 need to know which interfaces may still break before 1.0.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Build a physical input-to-photon measurement rig (photodiode plus microcontroller) and a pinned benchmark hardware set so latency claims are reproducible across releases.
rationale: Compositor and UI latency targets are meaningless without a measurement method independent of software timestamps.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Define the energy measurement methodology (external power meter, battery drain workloads, comparison OS images on the same laptop) before energy is tracked as a metric.
rationale: Energy is a listed tracked metric but is uniquely easy to mismeasure and must be defined before laptop targets are set.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Establish a fuzzing program for the native ABI (syzkaller-style descriptions generated from the IDL) that runs continuously from the first ABI prototype.
rationale: Kernel ABI bugs found after freeze become permanent compatibility hazards or CVEs.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the per-component page-table and huge-page policy for MemoryObjects and immutable package mappings after measuring startup and TLB effects.
rationale: The sub-20 ms startup target depends on how cheaply verified immutable pages can be mapped and shared.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the target hardware list for V1 through V2 (specific AMD desktop, Intel laptop, AMD laptop models) as an ADR before hardware-dependent spikes begin.
rationale: GPU, driver, energy and latency spikes all produce hardware-specific numbers and need a fixed reference set.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide how semantic interfaces are discovered and permissioned for automation and AI callers (per-interface capability grants, manifest-declared exposure, user consent flows) before any semantic interface is shipped.
rationale: Shipping semantic interfaces without a permission design would grant automation clients de facto ambient authority.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the dev environment implementation for services like Postgres (Linux personality OCI images, native packages, or both) after measuring the 50 ms cached startup target for each.
rationale: Most developer services exist only as Linux software, so the native environment story depends on this compatibility decision.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether ComputeDevice dispatch for GPUs is built over Vulkan compute, over a lower-level DRM job interface, or deferred until after 1.0.
rationale: Heterogeneous compute is a stated abstraction and the roadmap needs an explicit scope decision to avoid a half-built API in 1.0.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Publish a decision on the accessibility tree protocol (AT-SPI compatibility, a native semantic tree, or both) before the UI protocol freezes.
rationale: Accessibility metadata is required by the UI platform and existing assistive technology speaks AT-SPI.
